chapter: Bands, halls and the Smoky Mary
title: Playing dance halls and the back-room saloon dancing
summary: Glass recalls playing in a few places, including a back-room saloon run by Papa, and the interviewers ask about the district's dance halls.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Did you ever work in any of the dance halls in the district, much that you can remember?

Well, I played in two, three places. Played on Villery and Benville. I played in the back of the ballroom, the saloon there. Played back there. Played on St. Louis. Who ran that place on Villery and Benville?
Do you remember who ran that place?
Old fella, they used to call him Papa, I believe. He had some daughters, Papa.
So the back room of the saloon, did they have dancing there? Yeah, we did. Do you remember the entertainers there? It was on Franklin Street, what they call Crozat now, I guess.
Do you remember anything about the entertains, the hummingbirds, Black and Tans? No. I don't know. A few dance halls.
I understand in the very old days they didn't have many dance halls in the district at first, but that is where they had a whole band.
